dedupe_keys.name: usgs critical mineral deposits of the united states version 3 0 september 2026

description: This USGS database lists 1,271 mineral deposits in the United States documented to contain critical minerals, compiled for the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (Earth MRI) from the Mineral Resources Data System, the Alaska Resource Data File, USMIN, industry reports and literature. The ScienceBase page says deposits are classified by mineral system, deposit type and critical minerals present, with production and resource or reserve figures and references, and a rank from 1 to 5 based on past, current or potential production and known resources; 412 deposits have documented resources but no known production. Version 3.0, last revised on 9 September 2026 by Jane Hammarstrom, Laurel Woodruff and Connie Dicken, adds deposits for the 2025 USGS critical mineral list (boron, copper, lead, phosphate, potash, rhenium, silicon, silver and uranium among the additions) and keeps arsenic and tellurium. Files are an Excel workbook of all tables, a zipped GIS package, state and study region layers, a revision history and metadata, downloadable and free under CC0 1.0, with national coverage including Alaska. Caveats: metallurgical coal is not covered, and older resource figures may not meet current reporting codes. For simulation it gives the domestic critical mineral supply base for supply chain disruption and import dependence scenarios, and located sites for hazard exposure of future mines. Related catalogue records include the USGS Mineral Resources Data System, the USMIN commodity deposit releases and the USGS global critical minerals distribution.
